intent: How a value moved: an arrow and the signed change in success, danger or neutral text, with no fill.
useWhen: Which mark: Delta is how a value moved (arrow and sign, no fill, success or danger text). A money change is a Delta, never a Badge.
A money or metric change next to a value, like +$600 vs October
The change column in a table (kit Cell trendPositive / trendNegative)
The delta line on a KPI (kit Scorecard delta)
A change where up is bad, like cost or latency: pass goodWhen so the text says Better or Worse
doNotUseWhen: Status the system sets (Paid, Overdue) — use Badge
A label the user adds — use Tag
A whole KPI tile — use Scorecard

value.note: The visible change with its sign, e.g. +$600, −$90, +12.4% or No change. The sign or word carries the direction, so the arrow and colour are never the only signal.

direction.note: ArrowUp, ArrowDown or ArrowRight. flat is no change.

tone.note: Default from direction: up success, down danger, flat neutral. Override when up is bad (costs, churn) or down is good.

goodWhen.note: Which way a change is good: up (pass rate, revenue) or down (cost, latency). With direction up or down the text reads 'Better · +6.3 pts' with CircleCheck or 'Worse · +17%' with TriangleAlert, in place of the arrow. Only Worse carries colour (text-danger); Better stays neutral. tone still overrides the colour. flat is not judged. Words come from KitLabels better and worse.

size.note: sm is 12/16 caption with a 12px arrow, for dense rows. md is 14/20 with a 14px arrow.

requirements: The arrow and the Better/Worse icons are aria-hidden; the value text says the change and its sign
With goodWhen the Better or Worse word is in the visible text, so the icon and colour only repeat it
Colour is never the only signal: the arrow shape and the sign or word carry the direction
Amounts use tabular numbers so columns line up

doNot: Do not invent a local trend chip or coloured number
Do not use Badge for a money or metric change
Do not put a fill or border behind a Delta
Do not drop the sign from value; write +$600 or −$90, or No change
Do not add a second Better or Worse prefix to value; pass goodWhen
Do not use raw hex or primitive --color-* ramps
snippet:
<Delta value="+$600" direction="up" />
<Delta value="−$90" direction="down" />
<Delta value="No change" direction="flat" />
<Delta value="+$1,240" direction="up" tone="danger" />
<Delta value="+17%" direction="up" goodWhen="down" />
